candidates.tagline: Police post 'AI-enhanced' drug bust photo — AI helpfully converts $ to ¥
candidates.story: Vancouver Police Department posted an AI-edited social media photo of a June 2026 drug seizure on June 24, then deleted it after reporters noticed a visible 'Made with AI' watermark — and the AI had garbled all the cash amounts, converting Canadian dollars to '¥422.30' (a yen symbol) and '$.50.XX' on the official evidence labels.
candidates.why_funny: An official police evidence photo edited with AI to look more professional ended up inventing a Japanese yen-denominated drug bust.
candidates.alt: Two-panel AI-generated Vancouver Police evidence display on brown cardboard, showing seized drugs in plastic bags and Canadian cash, with AI-garbled handwritten labels including '¥422.30' using a yen symbol instead of Canadian dollars
candidates.license: editorial — © Vancouver Police Department / CTV News

candidates.tagline: Snap CEO calls $2,200 glasses 'highly wearable' while they crush his earlobes
candidates.story: Snap launched 'Specs' AR glasses on June 16, 2026 at $2,195 — CEO Evan Spiegel described them as 'highly wearable' at the launch event in footage that visibly shows the 136-gram chunky frames flattening his earlobes, the company's top Specs exec had already quit, and Snap stock fell ~10% on launch day.
candidates.why_funny: The CEO used himself as a live product demo to prove wearability and simultaneously demonstrated the opposite, on camera, at the launch event.
candidates.alt: Snap CEO Evan Spiegel wearing chunky oversized black Snap Specs AR glasses while being interviewed by TV camera at the 2026 Specs launch event, with 'SPECS' branding signage visible behind him
